Official Magnolia Hotels and CoralTree Hospitality webpages describe the Dallas property simply as 'Magnolia Dallas Downtown' with no Marriott, Hilton, IHG, Wyndham, Choice, Hyatt, or Best Western branding, confirming it has always been an independently branded boutique hotel rather than a major-chain franchise that could have 'lost' its flag.

In September 2021, CoralTree Hospitality, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Los Angeles-based real estate firm Lowe, acquired a controlling interest in the Magnolia Hotels brand; CoralTree directly manages four of the six original Magnolia hotels (Denver, Houston, St. Louis, Omaha) while licensing the Magnolia name to the Dallas and New Orleans properties. The hotel occupies the historic 1922 Magnolia Petroleum Company Building, a Dallas Landmark and National Register of Historic Places property topped by the iconic 'Pegasus' neon sign.

text.text: As a native of Dallas, I needed to stay closer to the city for a conference and chose The Magnolia Hotel based off of the pictures and Expedia reviews. I checked in and checked out literally within 20 min, knowing I wouldn't receive a refund. The room was listed as a Deluxe Queen Room. Upon walking into the room I noticed how old everything was. The lampshade had a hole in it. The furniture was worn. No comforter on the bed, only sheets. I felt like I was in a motel and not a hotel. The front desk staff was very monotone and unapologetic. There was NO concern whatsoever when I clearly checked in and out in less than 30 min. That was disappointing. I understand being Historic, but this was horrible.

text.text:
Our stay at Magnolia Hotel Dallas Downtown was very enjoyable overall. First, this is not a knock on the hotel itself, but downtown Dallas traffic is pretty horrible, so be prepared for that when arriving and leaving.

The hotel has a classic old-school feel that gives it a lot of character, and the old Mobil Oil décor throughout the property was a really nice touch. The staff was attentive, friendly, and helpful during our stay, which always makes a difference.

The rooms were comfortable, well-kept, and the bed was especially comfortable for a good night’s sleep. The room rate itself felt fair for the location and quality of the hotel, although the $50 per night parking charge seemed a bit high.

The location worked well for us since there were several very good restaurants nearby, and it provided a quick exit to the tollway the next morning. Overall, it was a comfortable stay with plenty of charm and a convenient downtown location.

text.text:
Let me say, I never leave reviews. But this was BAD. I wish I could leave negative stars

I will say, the lady at the front was quite helpful and very nice. But once I looked around I knew I made a mistake booking here.

We had pillows with makeup markings on them, towels that never got cleaned (hair, stains, parts were CRUNCHY).  The front lobby had a plaque stating rooms were cleaned every Tuesday and Friday. Clearly that wasn’t the case..

Windows had what looked like mold. Room smelled like there was either water damage somewhere, mothballs or mold.

We had trouble with the shower head and had to use our entire body weight to finally get it to start. The front desk asked if we were pulling it sideways to work, I said no as the instructions (that were taped to the highest point on the corner of the shower specifies NOT to do) She proceeded to pull it sideways for the water to come on…Seemed upset that I asked for help.

The hallways during our stay were filling up with used towels and garbage bags.

We only stayed two days as I had fully paid for this room in advance (via booking.com) and they charged me $100 for a deposit. The rest of the trip was great(because we weren’t in this room) but we will never stay here again as everything that was advertised was literally the opposite in terms of “boutique”. I felt gross the entire stay.

Very sad and disappointed. We are so excited to leave this place and go somewhere else.

text.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
I’ve had a wonderful experience at Alexis Hotel & Banquets and would absolutely recommend staying here.

Before I even booked, I called the front desk to ask about availability for a specific room type. The woman I spoke with was extremely helpful and kind, explaining what was available and guiding me on how to book it. When the exact option didn’t show online, she told me to leave a note on the reservation and reassured me everything would be taken care of — and it was. She also clearly explained the deposit amount ahead of time and let me know it could be paid in cash or by card, which helped a lot and made planning the trip much easier.

Check-in was quick and easy, and the staff has been genuinely friendly, caring, and funny. When we asked about coffee, the guy at the front desk jokingly said it would be $5-$10, then laughed and made the whole interaction light and fun. It was such a small moment, but it really showed how comfortable and welcoming the staff is here.

The hotel itself is a nice, cozy spot with a clean pool and a relaxed vibe. The vending machines are pretty funny too — the drinks are upside down in the machine new funny makes the hotel stand out and they come out upside down — but everything else has been great.

The location is another huge plus. It’s close to restaurants and right off the highway, making it very convenient. Even though it’s technically outside the city, you’re only about 15 minutes from downtown Dallas, which is perfect.

Overall, this has been a five-star stay. If you’re thinking about booking here, I definitely recommend calling the hotel directly — the staff is helpful, accommodating, and truly cares about making your stay easy and enjoyable. I would definitely stay here again!

Won’t be coming back to this one.

text.text:
So looking at past reviews it seems like nothing has changed and upper management doesn’t seem to take things seriously but I felt like I should at least give people a fair and honest review of this place because I paid close to $900 for the time I was there which is insane do to the pure disappointment of this hotel.

Starting with the front desk service. Three out of the four people I met at the front desk were wonderful people and I wish I had gotten all their names. 2 were girls and 1 guy. The one that had a lot of attitude and seemed to really hate her job had short-short hair and worked later afternoons. She always seemed annoyed. But the other three were top tier great people and super helpful and did their best with what they could.

It’s such a shame that the rooms couldn’t live up to the same level of the three wonderful customer service. Firstly, we had 1 working light and it was flickering 90% of the time in the bathroom and even after notifying front desk sadly nothing was done about it. There was even a spot where paint had been peeled off on the wall. Also, the bathtub/shower definitely looks like it needs to be resealed or something because it’s looking like it hasn’t been updated since being built. The water pressure is non existent and feels like little water droplets and takes forever to shower because rinsing off takes forever.

Now onto the room; there are stains EVERYWHERE. From the couch, desk chair, lamp shades, even on the carpet. When we first walked in it didn’t look cleaned AT ALL. There was water splashes on the mirror in the bathroom, dust on the desk by the tv and the desk by the bed, the carpet didn’t look vacuumed either. The beds had mattress toppers that had burn marks through them and sheets and blankets that had holes all over them. Which made me feel extremely uncomfortable that maybe there was a previous bug problem or rodent problem or maybe they hadn’t changed the sheets from the previous people staying there. I let the front desk know the room needed to be cleaned and they told me they will have them do a FULL cleaning. The house keeping changed the bedding but they didn’t actually fully clean like you’d expect. When coming back all they had done was bring more towels and replace the bedding. However, they didn’t clean the mirror because there were still water stains on it, didn’t wipe the desk down, didn’t vaccum, etc. The remaining of the trip I felt so uncomfortable, dirty, and was constantly looking for bed bugs or cockroaches or even mice. I barely got any sleep because I was feeling so grossed out.
Also, the outlets on the desk and the lamp by the beds don’t work and the few that did weren’t the best either.

Now, the area that it’s located is a good area with downtown being only 15/20 minutes away with some easy access to gas stations and other things around. We’ve previous stayed at the La Quinta last year and it was great. This year they sadly didn’t have availability during the time we needed.
Don’t be fooled by the photos provided by the hotel because I fell for it and when I saw it for my own eyes I was so disappointed and disgusted and extremely upset about spending $900.

I understand that remodels and updates cost money but this hotel really needs it. The upper management really needs to listen to the complaints because this location REALLY needs the attention. Especially for the price you’d expect to at least have a cleaned room.

It’s a shame that the front desk have to deal with ALL the complaints because it’s not their fault that upper management doesn’t care enough to fix the problems. All they can do is their best.

I’m definitely never staying here again and I will be contacting upper management for some sort of refund for having an incomplete room and disgusting excuse for a proper stay at a hotel. If they choose not to I will be filing a dispute with my bank and contacting some sort of health inspector to do a full run through of the hotel.

I highly suggest not staying here until upper management takes proper action into fixing all the problems.

Stayed at Days Inn Mesquite Rodeo, Texas from May 16 to May 18, and this was one of the worst hotel experiences I have ever had. I stayed for 2 days and completely regret booking this place.

The room was extremely dirty from the moment we entered. The floor looked like it had not been cleaned properly in a long time, and the overall condition of the room felt very poorly maintained. The worst part was the mosquitoes inside the room and around the bed area. It was impossible to relax or sleep comfortably because mosquitoes were constantly flying around and biting during the night.

The hygiene standards were unacceptable. The room did not feel fresh or sanitized, and it gave the impression that basic housekeeping was ignored. For a hotel that accepts paying guests, cleanliness should be the minimum expectation.

Customer service was also disappointing. Staff did not seem concerned about the issues, and there was little effort to improve the situation during the stay.

I would not recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a clean and comfortable place to stay. Very disappointing experience overall.

text.text: I would give this property 0 stars but it requires something. 1 Star is too generous. Front door is broken, homeless people sleeping on the couch and furniture in the "lobby." Noisy, extremely dirty, people are in and out all hours of the night slamming doors, fighting, pretty sure there's a prostitution or drug dealing thing going on in some of the rooms. Several shady looking guys going into one room constantly all night. The building is not secure, front desk is extremely rude. All you can smell in the hotel is marijuana and cigarette smoke. Guys were out in the hallway screaming and yelling at 2:30 am. I went down to the front desk to complain and no one was working. Went back upstairs and a bunch of drunk guys were in the hallway trying to intimidate me. I walked by and locked myself in my room. No elevator, had to drag my suitcase up a flight of stairs. In the 4 days that I stayed there, I got about 5 hours of sleep combined. Also, one night someone was trying to get into my room at about 3:30 am  This is a very slummy dangerous area. I will be reporting this hotel to their corporate.

text.text:
I wanted to like this location but our first room we got stank of old cigarette smoke. There were a million questionable stains, dead bugs, and holes everywhere from the walls, curtains, bed, and floor. There were cigarette burns, yellow stains on the bed sheets. Lots of holes in the curtain and the curtain doesn't fully cover the window all the way so weirdos are able to look inside of your room at an angle.

I don't think they ever clean the hard floor because my bare feet got instantly dirty when walking from one side of the room to the other.

When I left the room, I jiggled the door from the outside to make sure it was locked. If you force yourself through the door, it would unlock . I had to be at an event within 20 mins, but spent on an hour of moving everything to a new room. I had to go to the event, drop my partner off and then head back to the motel to make sure no one was breaking in our room. I informed the front desk and showed him how it was easy someone was able to get in with enough force. He wasn't convinced after 3 times when he closed the door and I was able to unlock it by force... Until the 4th time, he closed the door and I, again showed him how easy it was to force yourself in... Then he was convinced and I was able to change rooms. He was nice about the situation though.

Every time I left our room, I was worried that someone would break into our room. I didn't feel like I was in danger, but when you're not around and leaving your room to go out made me worry like crazy.

The accessible shower did not have any sort of shower chair, and I even called the front desk to ask and there was nothing. If my partner had not been traveling with me to physically support me, I likely would’ve hurt myself on the slippery tile trying to shower. Additionally, our air conditioner was old and busted and had to be turned back on every 10-20min, even throughout the night while we were trying to sleep. The room had a couch which was nice. The remote for the TV didn’t work and the tv was on when we got there so we had to unplug it to be able to sleep.

We had an amazing stay! From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere was welcoming and the hotel smelled incredible. Our room was very neat, clean, and well taken care of everything felt fresh and properly sanitized.

This is honestly one of the best hotels we’ve stayed at in a very long time. The attention to detail and cleanliness really stood out.

We also want to give a special thank you to the front desk lady who checked us in early Saturday morning around 1:00 AM. She was very sweet, professional, and took the time to answer all of our questions.

I kept telling my husband how amazing the hotel smelled and how clean everything was it made such a difference!

text.text:
La Quinta Inn, 380 E Palace Parkway, Grand Prairie, TX

This was one of the worst hotel experiences I’ve had. The room was not properly maintained, and several issues made the stay extremely uncomfortable.

First, the bed was very uncomfortable and made it difficult to get any rest. There were also burn holes in the blanket on the bed, which is completely unacceptable and shows a lack of attention to cleanliness and quality.

The bathroom lighting is connected to a master switch, so if the switch is turned off, you cannot turn the restroom light on. This is inconvenient and confusing, especially during the night.

The biggest issue was the air conditioning. I checked in around 3:00 PM and immediately set the AC to 62 degrees. The room never got cold and remained uncomfortable for hours. The AC did not start cooling properly until nearly 4:00 AM. Spending almost an entire night in a warm room was miserable.

For the price paid, I expected a clean, comfortable room with working amenities. Unfortunately, this hotel failed to meet even basic expectations. Between the uncomfortable bed, damaged bedding, poor room setup, and non-functioning air conditioning, I will never stay here again.

If management truly wants to make this right, a full refund would be appropriate.

Suggested title:
Terrible Stay – Uncomfortable Bed, Damaged Bedding, and AC Didn’t Work

text.text:
I had a very disappointing experience at this La Quinta hotel.

After checking in, we dropped off our bags, went out to run a few errands, and then had dinner. When we returned to our room that evening, we immediately noticed that the air conditioning unit was extremely loud. The noise was constant and made it very difficult to relax, let alone sleep.

I contacted the front desk and spoke with Mayra, who told me there was nothing they could do. I tried to tolerate the noise and get some rest, but it became impossible. I later requested to be moved to another room, but was told the hotel was completely full. Based on the circumstances, I did not feel that I was being given an honest effort to resolve the issue.

By approximately 11:30 p.m., after several unsuccessful attempts to deal with the situation, we decided to leave the hotel and find another place to stay for the night. Considering that I had to work the following day, the last thing I wanted was to move hotels in the middle of the night, but the room conditions left us with no other reasonable option.

Later, I received a call from Manager Reyna Trujillo, who informed me that they had determined there was nothing wrong with the air conditioning unit and that no other guests had complained about it. I found this response dismissive and unprofessional. Just because other guests may not have complained does not mean the issue did not exist. I had already reported the problem earlier in the evening and requested assistance, yet no meaningful accommodation was offered.

What was most frustrating was feeling as though my concerns were being dismissed rather than addressed. If the issue was not real, why would we voluntarily leave the hotel late at night and pay for another hotel just to get some sleep?

Customer service is about listening to guests and trying to find solutions. Unfortunately, neither Mayra nor Reyna demonstrated that level of professionalism or concern. I travel to Texas frequently, but after this experience, I will not be staying at this property again.

Traveling to Ennis, TX. I booked a room at the motel 6 in Lancaster. It’s located close to great western inn. The room smelled clean and fresh, but not of cleaner… just fresh. There was fresh carpet, clean and comfortable queen beds, a desk, dresser, fridge and microwave. It never once felt unsafe. This seems like a place where working men who travel go to stay.

We will be back in a year for the next race at Texas Motorplex and this will be where we stay.

The swimming pool was closed for no obvious reason. When we asked about it we were only told pool is closed indefinitely.

text.text:
Overall our stay was good (free parking and hot buffet breakfast, easy access to Hwy 635, nice and professional staff).

We needed a place, close to Dallas , to stay for the night. We planned to wake up early in the morning, just in time to have breakfast at 6:30 AM, and leave shortly after. However, our schedule got a little messed up when we were going to take a shower and there was not hot water. We waited for 10 minutes and nothing. So we had to take a quick shower with cold water to try to stay on schedule. After 20 minutes of letting the water run it was when it finally got hot.

This was very disappointing and stressful…

We informed the front desk staff about the hot water issue. The gentleman who was there at that time say he’ll let the manager know.

Lesson learned! Upon arrival at the hotel room, always check for hot water.

text.text:
As someone who previously worked as a flight attendant, I have had the opportunity to stay in more hotels than most and understand very well the difference between good service and poor service. Unfortunately, this property did not meet even basic standards, let alone exceed expectations.

Upon arrival, everything seemed fine. However, on the second day of my six-day stay, I had a very uncomfortable experience. As I pulled into the parking lot and was gathering my belongings to exit my car, I was suddenly approached and cornered by an overly aggressive security guard who demanded that I prove I was a guest. I had just arrived and had not even stepped away from my vehicle. After this encounter, I felt targeted, singled out, and genuinely uneasy about my safety.

I immediately reported the incident to the front desk, but no action was taken. The following morning, I received a survey via text and again described my experience with security. I received no response until I followed up myself a day later, asking why management had not contacted me after such a concerning incident. Only then did the manager respond — and even that follow-up felt delayed and insufficient. Even when I spoke with the manager in person on the morning of my departure, I was essentially told there was no reason to follow up with me — despite the fact that I was the one who experienced the incident.

To be fair, Amy was wonderful, and so was the night time front desk associate was also kind and helpful. However, isolated positive interactions were not enough to outweigh the overall experience, which left me feeling very dissatisfied.

Beyond the security issue, the overall condition of the hotel reflected a lack of care. There was vomit in the hallway that I first noticed on day two, and it remained there for the duration of my stay, still present when I checked out. There was also broken glass in the parking lot. Elevator #2 was unreliable — it made loud noises, shook noticeably, and felt unsafe to ride. Additionally, the inspection certificate inside the elevator appeared altered, which raised further concerns about maintenance and safety.

The heating system was inconsistent and difficult to manage, requiring constant adjustment just to maintain a comfortable temperature.

While the hotel advertises complimentary breakfast, the quality was extremely poor. The options were limited, unappealing, and poorly maintained — far below what even a budget property should provide. It felt like an afterthought rather than a service offered with care.

Overall, this was a two-star experience at best, and I would strongly recommend staying elsewhere. To the manager who failed to properly address this situation: service culture starts at the top. As someone in management myself, I understand that a team reflects its leadership. This situation should have been handled promptly and professionally, and it was not. I will also be sharing my experience with my employer, as this level of service does not deserve continued business support.

text.text: For whatever reason the hotels in this area were much higher than usual. This one was the nicest looking for the price point. I checked in with a woman at the front desk & went to my room & there was an entire family in there. Somehow the lady at the front desk managed to give me an occupied room. LUCKY for me they were sleeping otherwise who knows that could’ve played out for me. I then went back downstairs & the lady said she was a little dyslexic & wrote the wrong room # down……kind of a big mistake. But I brushed it off. Around 11 pm I hear a lot of commotion outside. I look out the window (pic attached) to see maybe 15 girls dancing with a very loud speaker. I call the front desk. He said he’d check on what was going on. It stopped for a bit then immediately started back up. I called the front desk yet again. His response this time was “I already went out there”…..okay?? And?? It’s still going on! Shortly after that call around 1 am it did finally stop. The next day I check my credit card & I see I have a pending incidental charge which I knew about. Then I saw a random pending charge. I waited a few days to see if they’d fall off. The incidental did, however the other did not. I called the hotel & the man on the phone informed me this random charge was for “stained towels”. I was so confused because all I did was take a shower. Nothing crazy. I asked if he could send pics so I could see what he could possibly be referring to. He said he would have them sent over. I called 3x & I have still not received these photos. I also emailed the manager because at this point it is ridiculous to think it’s appropriate to charge me for “stained towels” after all the bs I went through!!! If I don’t hear back I will be disputing this charge with my bank.

Rooms were good sized after being upgraded to a suite for a one night weekday stay. However the suite itself definitely seemed like it could use some more cleaning, HVAC had a musty smell which definitely detracted. Not enough lighting for such a large room. Bathroom tiny and old for such a space. Did find a hair on the bed and missing conditioner and body wash from the bulk bottles (they were just not attached to the wall).

Some highlights: good service recovery when I responded to the service manager asking how my stay was. The breakfast was included in my corporate rate and was good quality. Fresh cooked to order omelette, fresh blackberries, smoked salmon and the usual continental breakfast fixings. Service was a little slow but it since it's mostly a buffet, it wasn't too bad.

text.text: The room was fine, aside from the toilet being crazy loud and the door of the room being really squeaky. We liked the room and the staff were friendly but all on their personal phones having personal conversations in front of guests. I could tell you 2 employees entire conversations with friends/family because they were having them right in front of me as they checked me out and another employee as I walked down the hallway past them. But the real issue was the pool. We came from out of state to bring my husband, who travels for work, his new plate tag. We were only here for 1 night, and the only “fun” thing the kids were gonna do and were so excited to do, was the pool. They were literally begging me all morning to go down. We finally went down after I called to confirm the time the pool was open, which front desk said 10, only for our key not to work and staff to tell us the pools not open for the entire day. How absolutely disappointing. We got this hotel specifically for the outdoor pool. Don’t charge pull price for a hotel that doesn’t have all amenities available when expected. It’s extremely upsetting that my kids had to be disappointed like this.

text.text:
Personally, my favorite hotel in Dallas. The staff are always kind and attentive. I personally like the food that they serve for breakfast even though it's not to everyone's taste. Their location is unbeatable since they're right next to the Walmart, the Sonic, Wingstop, a freaking car wash, and even a Taco Bell. All within walking distance, and you can't find that anywhere else.

Cherry on top of the cake is that they only charge literally 25 bucks for incidentals... A lot of hotels that I went to charge $100 outright just to be able to lay down. It's kind of an all-in-one and so much more when it comes to the hotel mixed with its location. My personal favorite, but pick what you think is right for you at the end of the day. 🤙🏿

text.text:
I do NOT recommend this hotel.

During my stay there was constant noise all nights I stay for almost a month, making it almost impossible to sleep. If you are looking for a quiet place to rest, this is definitely not it.

On top of that, they charged $25 to my card without my consent for alleged damage in the room. When I checked in, I had already informed the front desk about damages that were already present, and the staff acknowledged they were aware of them. I even took photos of the room beforehand specifically to avoid situations like this.

The issue they mentioned about a missing glass was already resolved because the glass was returned. Despite this, they still kept the charge. I contacted them by email and was told the money would be refunded, but the refund was never issued.

This hotel also advertises itself as an “extended stay,” yet the room or front desk did not have basic kitchen items like pots or other essentials you would normally expect.

Overall, this was a very frustrating and disappointing experience due to the constant noise, the unauthorized charge, and the fact that they promised a refund but never followed through.

text.text:
A Mid-Century Modern Gem in Downtown Dallas
From the moment you pull up to The Statler, you know you are in for a unique experience. The retro, mid-century modern aesthetic is perfectly captured right at the entrance, where a rotating display of gorgeous, classic cars parked out front sets a fun, nostalgic vibe before you even step through the doors. It is the perfect nod to the hotel’s historic 1950s roots while feeling completely fresh and upscale.
What really makes the experience stand out, though, is the staff. Despite the hotel's sleek, historic grandeur, every single team member—from the valet to the front desk—is incredibly down-to-earth, warm, and attentive. There is absolutely zero pretension here; just genuine hospitality that makes you feel immediately welcome.
Epic Eats and Entertainment at Scout
The absolute highlight of the entertainment options on-site is Scout, the hotel's massive, high-energy social hall. It is a fantastic spot to unwind, featuring a fantastic vintage-style bowling alley right inside. Knocking down pins with a drink in hand is the ultimate way to spend an evening without ever having to leave the property.
The food and drink at Scout are equally exceptional. The Texas Burger is an absolute must-try—a massive, mouthwatering double patty stacked with perfectly melted pepper jack cheese, crispy onion rings, and a rich BBQ sauce that delivers a true taste of the Lone Star State. Pair it with one of their signature, expertly balanced margaritas, and you have a flawless meal.
Whether you are looking for a lively night of bowling and great food, spectacular downtown energy, or just a comfortable stay handled by an amazing crew, The Statler delivers on every front. I will definitely be back!

text.text:
I stayed in Room 709 for my birthday weekend 5/29-30 , and overall I had a really good stay. The hotel is absolutely beautiful. The pictures online look great, but they honestly don’t do it justice. My room was amazing, the view was everything, and one of the main reasons I booked this hotel was because of the soaking tub.

I do want to mention one issue I had with housekeeping. When I arrived, there was hair in the tub. Not gonna lie, that was pretty disgusting. Nobody wants to arrive at their room and find someone else’s hair in the tub, especially when the soaking tub was one of the things I was most looking forward to using during my stay. I reached out to the front desk, and housekeeping came up. Unfortunately, it seemed like they only removed the hair instead of actually cleaning and sanitizing the tub. The tub was still dry and didn’t appear to have been cleaned at all. What really stood out to me was that Morgan from the front desk ended up making sure the tub was properly cleaned while I was away at my event. I appreciated that more than she knows, but honestly, that shouldn’t have fallen on her. Housekeeping should have taken care of it correctly the first time.

Now, I want to give Morgan, Skylar, and Josue their flowers because they were absolutely amazing. Morgan was helpful before I even checked in. She answered my questions through the chat, was always kind, and made me feel taken care of before I ever stepped foot in the hotel. Then, while I was getting ready for an event at the Majestic Theatre, I had a wardrobe malfunction and thought my whole birthday weekend was about to be ruined. Skylar came up to help, Morgan stepped in to help, and they even got Josue involved. The teamwork between the three of them was incredible. They didn’t have to go out of their way for me, but they did, and their kindness and genuine customer service meant a lot.

The housekeeping issue definitely needs attention because something as simple as checking and properly cleaning a tub before a guest arrives can make a huge difference. But I also don’t want this review to go by without recognizing Morgan, Skylar, and Josue. They truly went above and beyond, and they played a big part in making my solo birthday weekend special. Thank you all for your kindness and for making me feel cared for during my stay.

text.text:
Overall, not a bad hotel, but the experience definitely felt more “Carnival Cruise” than luxury hotel.

We arrived before check-in and went up to the rooftop pool around 2:20 PM since rooms weren’t available until 4:00. The rooftop pool itself was honestly overhyped compared to the photos online. The website makes it look much more luxurious than it actually feels in person. There was a DJ and definitely more of a party atmosphere, but we were surprised to hear reserved seating was around $250 (if I heard correctly). Because of that vibe, we ended up going to the second pool instead, which was calmer and honestly more enjoyable. It was nice, just not much of a view.

At 4:00 PM we went to check in, and that was probably the worst part of the experience. The woman working the front desk came across like she absolutely hated her job and acted irritated the entire interaction. We had already prepaid for our room through Expedia, but they still didn’t even have a room ready for us at check-in time.

Once we finally got into the room, we immediately noticed a mold/mildew smell. Later on, we could also smell weed smoke coming through the vent from another room nearby.

The hotel itself has a cool atmosphere and the historic building is unique, but between the misleading marketing photos, check-in experience, and room issues, it just didn’t really feel like the upscale luxury experience we expected.

text.text:
Rooms ending in 32 or 33 are notably compact. These particular rooms were not included in the recent hotel renovations. A 28-inch suitcase may be challenging to fully open within these accommodations. However, these rooms do offer desirable corner views, featuring expansive windows that provide a panoramic perspective. All even-numbered rooms from 02-12 and 24-32 have an obstructed view. For guests prioritizing a scenic outlook, alternative room selections are recommended. The bedding consists of softer, "sink-in" style mattresses and exceptionally plush pillows, which may not appeal to all preferences.

The speakeasy venue presented an issue with fruit flies; I personally addressed two, and a third was observed in active flight. Upon inquiry, a staff member acknowledged the persistent nature of the problem, indicating that trap deployment and drain cleaning efforts had been undertaken with limited success. The "sports bar" is primarily a bar area equipped with pool tables, cornhole, and a two-lane bowling alley. It was noticeably understaffed, with a single bartender managing both drink and food orders, and also responsible for delivering food orders to the restaurant and retrieving them due to the absence of a runner or bar back.

text.text:
Our stay unfortunately started off on the wrong foot, as we had to request two room changes upon arrival. The first room had a persistent high-pitched noise coming from the TV which was difficult to ignore. After reporting it, we were moved to a second room, but it was clear it had not been properly prepared despite being labeled as “ready.” There was an unfolded hand towel left by the sink, and the bed linens appeared used, which made us uncomfortable.

Thankfully, the third room we were assigned was clean and problem-free, and we were able to settle in without further issues. Expect for the fact that we had NO HOT WATER one night and the receptionist didnt seem to really care once I brought it to their attention. Another thing to note, is that no matter what room in the hotel you are in, expect to hear frequent outside noise as the hotel is located in a busy downtown area.

We were disappointed with the lack of communication regarding benefits from the American Express Hotel Collection. Typically, we receive a clear explanation or written summary of the included credits, but that was not provided during this stay. Additionally, even after combining our Amex booking with our Hilton Diamond status, the level of service did not feel consistent with what we would expect at that tier.

On a positive note, the dining options at the hotel were excellent. Every restaurant we tried exceeded expectations, and the speakeasy was easily one of the most unique and enjoyable bar experiences we’ve had, we highly recommend. While we didn’t have the chance to dine at the rooftop bar, we heard great feedback from other guests, and the views alone make it a worthwhile spot to visit.

text.text: Ask for a non-smoking room at check-in and told all rooms are non-smoking. When I entered the room, the cigarette smell was overwhelming. I had brought  my own blankets and pillows because I didn’t want to sleep in the cover. The refrigerator in room doesn’t shut and was frozen up with a 6 in of ice, so no way to have food. AC was cold and water was hot, plus for that!! Our AC at home was being replaced and I needed a place that accepted my dogs. When we checked out and left all my belongings smelled horribly, that I had to leave them in my garage, bringing in one load to wash at a time. Even my glasses smelled. I travel for a living so I understand getting what you pay for, but I can’t ever go back due to the nasty smell. On the second day there, I brought my Clorox wipes, Clorox clean up, and swifter. In the end they should have paid me to stay there; I am sure the room hasn’t been that clean in a long time, but no matter how much you clean you can’t cover cigarette smoke infused curtains, ac unit, and mattresses. Again, we had cold ac and nice hot shower and my doggies were able to cool down, so we made it work. Lmbo my husband chose to stay at our house with no ac, he said he just couldn’t handle the smell. I don’t appreciate being placed in that room after specifically asking for non smoking. I’m also kinda pissed no one even mentioned coffee or breakfast snacks.

After a long day of driving on the busy highways. This stay was well appreciated.

text.text:
This property really needs to get its act together when it comes to elite recognition and communication. They operate one service desk for both the Residence Inn and the AC Hotel, but the staff clearly hasn’t been trained on the different brand policies.
As a Titanium Elite guest staying 6 nights at the Residence Inn, I was told at check-in that I would receive a 10$ market coupon for each day. On the 3rd day, another associate told me it wasn’t $10, but instead one free market item per night. Fine until checkout, when I was suddenly informed that it was only a one-time free market item at check-in. That’s three different stories in less than a week.
To make matters worse, I was billed for items I was initially told were complimentary. I had to call multiple times just to get in touch with a manager because no one would return my calls.
This lack of consistency and accountability is completely unacceptable, especially for a Marriott property. Titanium Elite members (or any guest, really) should not be given the runaround like this.
On a positive note, the housekeeping team did an excellent job, my room was spotless throughout the stay. Unfortunately, the front desk issues overshadowed what could have been a good experience.

text.text:
I feel like a lot of the reviews for this hotel are misleadingly good or bad.   So I'll share my impressions in the hopes that anyone who chooses to stay here is making the best choice.

GOOD:   This is a newer property, and it's in pretty good shape.   The rooms are tasteful and well-laid out.   The pool is pleasant - not gross like at so many other hotels at this price point.   I was also particularly pleased with the staff, who were all extremely friendly and helpful.    The location might not be useful for everyone, but at least it's convenient to get to from the Tom Landry Freeway.   Decent size parking lot.

MEH:  One of the problems with staying here is absolutely no fault of the hotel:   This neighborhood sucks.   The two restaurants adjacent to the hotel are both pretty terrible, and there is nothing else within walking distance.   The Olive Garden is OK if you have children or elderly parents, but is otherwise not a very fun place to go.   And the Buffalo Wild Wings was absolutely disgusting -- the garbage smell in there was so horrible I had to leave before even sitting down.    There is a Starbucks, and I appreciate that.   But that's absolutely it.

I was charged for parking on my bill at checkout and the staff corrected it.   I don't think anyone was trying to cheat me.   What I think happened here is that no one ever stays at this hotel without a car.   And I can certainly see why.

I also thought the breakfast they offer at this hotel is pretty lackluster.   All four days I was there was the same:  the usual wet eggs, sad chicken sausage discs, Jimmy Dean microwave sandwiches, oatmeal, and a little bit of fruit.    Not horrible, but could be a lot better.

BAD:   The real shame of this hotel is that they are built directly over one of the loudest highways in America, but their building has absolutely no modern soundproofing.   You will hear the Tom Landry Freeway in your room 24x7.    I was able to somewhat sleep through it.   But you can't really enjoy the pool or any other common spaces at the hotel without being bombarded by the noise.    I've stayed at other hotels by highways, including a Hilton property along this same highway, and they all had various degrees of soundproofing.   This hotel was clearly built on the cheap, and I doubt there's anything that can be done about it.

I have been to several Hampton Inns, but this is the worst one i've been in.

Don't get me wrong:  The room was ALMOST like all the other Hamptom Inns i've ever been in.  The rooms were clean, but the pillows are god-awful and the shower pressure was mediocre.  The other Hampton Inns i've been in had nothing to complain about in the room.

When i've exited out the west exit, i noticed that one of the doors were literally broken off, allowing bugs and wasps to enter freely.

Wifi is very slow unless you pay for the faster connection.

The coffee in the front desk is either empty, or lukewarm/cold.  No attention was paid to the coffee.  No cold water to dispense other than inside the workout room.

Location is full of impatient cars wizzing about.  Plenty of places to eat, but you will need a ride to get there.

Breakfast is no different than one you would get from La Quinta Inn.  No bacon.  Mediocre scrambled eggs and round sausage patties with potatos.  No different from La Quinta Inn.  Also, all the drinks only spouted out water.  No orange/apple juice or any other drinks other than water coming out.

It just seems like attention to detail is lacking here at this location.

Would i ever stay here again?  No.  Why would anyone do that?  You can get a room at La Quinta for significantly less money and basically get the exact same thing. The only thing this Hampton has above other 2-star hotels is the pool and workout room.  If you aren't into that, just go grab a 2-star hotel that costs less.

text.text:
So Google family.....once more I am online one wonderful day, searching for a reasonable and "un-janky" room on a busy pre-fourth holiday weekend and mind you I am on priceline....so I come across the Scottish Inn with a total of 77.97 with no listing of hotel deposit right? Looks decent enough that with detail of having a nice breakfast so I book it. Something dawns on me to call and check for a deposit and Melissa said 25.00 due upon check in cash or charge right? Don't sound too bad so I go for it.

When I check in Akil does his best but hasn't quite built rapport with me and put me in a room after making some adjustments and I am in for the night.

But am informed of NO BREAKFAST and not even coffee. So yes Google family they have no breakfast. They have snacks and soda at the front desk for two and three dollars. Laundry facilities looks to be about 1.50 to 2.00 and ice machine is there. Wifi is basic and there are huge hornets by the door so don't have your kids out there in the day time. There is an ice cream vending machine outside in front with most stuff 2 and 3 dollars.

Next day even though I called back and informed Emily of my business endeavors which she was also kind, the manager Deepa takes over.

She is very unprofessional and talks extremely fast with no respect and gets irritated with having to accommodate. She put me in another room because of all the bathtub bugs you see in the picture.  After going off on me by phone of my business meeting running late we when got there a little after 1230 which the front desk staff was made aware of this during check in so that phone call was maniacal in itself.  After finally checking in the second day she put me in a terrible dog smelling room with a leaky sink and more bugs,  I had to spray the curtains and beds and walls to keep from being nauseous.  The dog smell was so bad the neighborhood dogs followed me around when I walked to the store.  And when asking for clean sheets when the double bed room ( claiming that was all the rooms they had) had stains and makeup on the sheets,  she ensured me they were clean and got more irritated like I was a problem and even though I had reservations for two more nights she wanted me to check out early and wanted me off the property.

So Google family I posted pics as proof but that 77.97 came with a price.

To HIHotels International Hospitality Group, I am praying for the manager lady named Deepa to get better at her "care" of people spending their hard earned money that need someone to lay their heads. This world is very unique and the struggle is already real. Last thing people need is being treated like that if they spending money at your business.

text.text: The only positive things I can say about this hotel is the staff were friendly and understanding and the breakfast was hot. That being said, the hotel is not worthy of the Marriott name. To begin with, as we were walking to our room we noticed several rooms appeared to have their doors forced open and they were not shutting completely or securely. The hallways were in various states of disrepair needing both painting and wallpaper replaced. The first room we were given had substantial water damage at some point and was not properly repaired. The room was not clean and had a weird smell that didn’t appear to be from the water damage. The furniture was mix matched and there was a very suspicious stain on the shower curtain. After speaking with staff we were gratuitously moved to a new room. While the room was better, it appeared to not have been vacuumed and the furniture was mismatched. The bed was cheap and uncomfortable. We had reserved a room for a week but only stayed for two nights before changing hotels. I would not recommend this hotel.

text.text:
I had a very disappointing stay at this hotel. The walls are extremely thin, and noise from neighboring rooms carries very easily. I barely got any sleep due to loud noise coming from a nearby room. I called the front desk to complain and was told someone would be sent to check, but even after waiting over an hour, nothing changed and the noise continued. I eventually had to handle the situation myself by asking the neighboring room to keep it down, which should never be a guest’s responsibility.

I am a Gold member with Marriott, yet no upgrades or added benefits were offered. When I asked for a bottle of water at check-in, the front desk staff was noticeably rude. I was also told I would be charged $50 for a late checkout, with the manager claiming housekeeping would need to work overtime. This explanation felt unprofessional and came across as an excuse to charge an unnecessary fee rather than provide standard loyalty benefits.

To make matters worse, the hotel was completely out of parking upon arrival. Overall, this stay fell well below expectations and felt like poor business practices aimed at taking advantage of guests rather than providing hospitality. I do not recommend this hotel and would not stay here again.

text.text: The only positive about this hotel is that the location is very central to most touristy places (short car ride). That's the main reason why I booked this hotel with my Marriott points for a first stay in Dallas. I should have read these reviews, because it was not a relaxing place to spend a vacation. The lobby is the nicest part of this hotel. The rest is very subpar from the typical Marriott experience. I'm a Gold Bonvoy member, and even though I am supposed to have automatic upgrades, none were offered. The original room that we were assigned was already occupied, so we had to go back down to the lobby. They are doing remodeling, which is desperately needed, but they did nothing to help accommodate guests. There was exposed ducts and electrical wiring in the hallway ceiling. The second floor and our room stunk. The room itself was the most sad, creepy, and depressing hotel room I have ever been in, and I travel a lot. Concrete everything... Floor, walls, all cold concrete, which was cracked and chipped in many places. I think the vibe was supposed to be urban industrial, but with the current execution the room literally felt like a spacious prison cell. Turning on the sink usually resulted in a very strong unpleasant odor, much like spoiled eggs or sewage. Our view was of a parking garage. The pool was right below our room, and if anyone wants to use the pool, you will be subjected to hearing them until 11 pm, when the pool closes. In addition, oddly enough, the wall separating the rooms with the bed headboard? The one thing that is not concrete, so you will hear and feel anything your neighbors do. If I ever have to stay in Dallas again, I will not be staying here.

text.text:
The room was clean and the staff were really helpful and nice. Parking can be confusing, so make sure if you park where it says Platinum you let the staff members know. They will charge you inside the hotel. Do not pay the fee outside and inside-the hotel will give you a discounted rate for 24hrs. I made a mistake and paid double but the staff members gave me a refund without a problem.

The only complaint I have is that there was a weird smell in the room. I could not pin point what it was because the room was in fact clean. I should had let a staff member know but it wasn't that strong. Other than that everything was great. The view was great and the TV worked without problems. I checked in and out without any difficulty.  They do have karaoke nights and a bar at the bottom. This is great if you want ambience.

I initially thought I had lost my wallet after leaving my Uber ride, and I was panicking at the front desk. The staff there urgently assisted me in trying to contact my Uber, but unfortunately, there was no success. Thankfully, I later discovered that I had hidden my wallet in my laptop bag.

I cannot express enough how grateful I am for the front office team who went above and beyond to help me. They assisted me in various ways, from helping me log into my Uber account to calling customer service, and even reaching out to my Uber driver directly. I was relieved to find my wallet safe and secure in my laptop bag.

I want to extend my heartfelt thanks to Asa for his calm and welcoming demeanor, and to Khristian for his prompt support. Both gentlemen were truly among the best staff I have ever encountered during a hotel stay, great restaurant choice btw! Lastly, Emily, the manager, helped in every way possible, and I appreciate all of you more than words can express!

text.text:
This hotel was perfect for my last minute stay (I booked around 440 and checked in at 530). The front desk attendants that I interacted with (Christian and another taller, black guy on my Saturday night and an older black guy on Sunday at checkout) were extremely kind, professional and personable.

The hotel lobby is quite large (including a bar-I didn’t get to try, a pool table, sitting areas, grab and go breakfast cafe-didn’t try but it was pricey, gym-nice and clean) The room was clean and roomy with a decent view, the ironing board is pretty short and my toilet had issues flushing at times but it was nothing that would deter me from booking again. Overall, I enjoyed my stay here and it was conveniently located as well, I was able to walk safely and solo to the AT@T Discovery Center. Parking was $17 daily through the hotel and $30 through the actual lot so that was a nice deal. The parking lot was huge but a little ways from the front door. However, they do have carts and up front parking for overnight guests when they don’t fill up. They also have nightly entertainment in the lobby from a solo guitar player… also, the bathroom door is the side mirror and it slides (took me a second to realize that)

text.text:
I chose this hotel because of the proximity to my job during the recent bout of Texas ice storms, and the affordability. This is an older property, but I thought the rooms were clean and I felt safe (traveling alone as a woman). Overall, I would definitely feel comfortable staying here again!

Yarizet (I know I spelled her name wrong), the overnight receptionist, was amazing. She was has a kind demeanor, answered all of my questions, and helped me get things squared away when part of my reservation was canceled due to a late check in. She greeted me each night when I came back from work, and that meant a lot to me.

For out of towners— I know a lot of the reviews mention car theft. I can’t speak into that as it was not a problem during my stay. They share a parking lot with a slightly more expensive hotel, and I did not have issues with my car when I stayed there previously. There are security officers patrolling both lots in their cars overnight. The location seems convenient on paper, but this is not the best part of town, so keep that in mind when booking!

text.text:
Was a typical Fairfield Inn experience at first, nothing to write home about, I was just here on business and don’t usually stay in this part of town, but it was a pretty sad part of town. No real restaurants, only chains and pretty isolated from other parts of the city. My room, which was on level with some type of awning/roof (floor 2), I noticed there was trash on this awning, including a weed pen tip with drug residue still inside. Overall, I would’ve considered staying here again, since the room was adequate, but that was gross and a bad look for the hotel.

However, on the night of my last stay, people crawled through their windows so they could walk on the awning and smoke weed. I was sitting getting ready for bed, when my room reeked of marijuana. I saw a hooded figure standing at my window (very, very alarming) and then that person turned around. I attempted to call the front desk, who completely ignored my phone call for 5 minutes. I went back to bed but will never stay at this particular Fairfield again. It is not appropriate or safe to allow your guests to walk around a two story roof, watch young women from outside their window, while doing drugs that are illegal in TX and leave the trash around your property. It was disturbing to me that no security or front desk agent was available to ask those individuals to stop and/or move me to a safer room.
